title: Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun
lead: The three Levite families of musicians who, according to Chronicles, Ezra and Nehemiah, led the singing of the Temple from David's day on. Their names stand in the titles of many psalms.

sections.b: Chronicles traces the Temple choirs to David. When the ark came to Jerusalem, the Levites appointed Heman, Asaph and Ethan to lead with cymbals, lyres and harps (1 Chronicles 15:16–24), and David set Asaph before the ark and Heman and Jeduthun at the altar in Gibeon (1 Chronicles 16:4–7, 37–42). Later he organized their sons into twenty-four groups (1 Chronicles 25). Heman descends from Kohath, Asaph from Gershom, and Ethan (perhaps the same as Jeduthun) from Merari (1 Chronicles 6:33–47). The singers return in the stories of Solomon's dedication, Jehoshaphat's battle and Hezekiah's and Josiah's reforms, and the "sons of Asaph" were among the exiles who came home (Ezra 2:41; Nehemiah 7:44).

sections.b: Twelve psalms carry Asaph's name (Psalm 50; 73–83). Psalm 88 is linked with Heman the Ezrahite and Psalm 89 with Ethan the Ezrahite, and Jeduthun appears in the headings of Psalms 39, 62 and 77. Heman and Ethan are also famous wise men in 1 Kings 4:31. Many scholars think these psalm collections were handed down by the singer guilds of the Second Temple, and that Chronicles describes their order as it stood in the writer's own day; traditional readers take Chronicles' account of David's arrangements at face value.
